summary: Cauchy–Schwarz over 𝗆^F_j and two applications of lintegral_mul_invWeight_le.

steps.lean: obtain ⟨k, k'⟩ := Γ.isPairingKernel_self hk _, Γ.isPairingKernel_translatePairing hk hk' ..
steps.claim: The two pairing kernels k and k'.

steps.lean: obtain ⟨b, c⟩ := k.weightedSquareSum_invariant_support x, k'.weightedSquareSum_invariant_support x
steps.claim: Their weighted square sums at floor j are Q_j-invariant and vanish off near points.

steps.lean:
nth_grw 1 [selfNormProduct, ← k.selfNorm_le_selfNorm_zero hj.step, sq_lintegral_le,
    lintegral_stackMeasure_mul_left p, stackMeasure_zero_eq,
    Γ.lintegral_mul_invWeight_le hj hp hx .refl c, lintegral_const_mul (K * Γ.globalConst),
    stackMeasure_zero_eq, Γ.lintegral_mul_invWeight_le hj hp.star_head hx .refl b] <;> try fun_prop
steps.claim: selfNorm(F, 0, …) ≥ selfNorm(F, j, …); Cauchy–Schwarz on 𝗆^F_j with the two factors; translate by w_j(p)⁻¹ (lintegral_stackMeasure_mul_left); write 𝗆^F_j = ascConv(η, j) ∗ θ-part and bound each factor with lintegral_mul_invWeight_le (for p and for p*).
w_j(p) commutes with H_j; invariance of the second factor.

steps.lean: intro g; by_cases e : f g = 0; simp [e]
steps.claim: Pointwise in g: if f(g) = 0 there is nothing to prove.

steps.lean: grw [hf g e]; simp [invWeight, Set.indicator]; split_ifs; ring_nf; repeat simp [*]
steps.claim: Otherwise use hf and the definition of invWeight (the indicator of the near points).
